body:
SWEEP OF THE SAME SHAPE OUTSIDE align, on main 185380b. cursor-grok-storymodel4s swept
signature.scala and found three (bd-01M17AS0BGAW9CF6VFHST9JMY3); nobody had swept the rest of
the repository. I did, read every tolerance constant in main sources, and verified each in
source. Two real instances, one negligible, and one that is the CORRECT pattern and should be
the template.

INSTANCE 1 -- interview/scoring/Resolution.scala:100-106. The strongest, because it is
identical to the ExternalMassReport case grok found in a different module:

    if math.abs(total - 1.0) > Tolerance then Left(...) else <store parts unchanged>

resolved + unresolved + excluded is a THREE-WAY PARTITION OF UNITY. The guard decides "this
sums to one" and then stores three numbers that sum to 1 +/- 1e-9. Same shape, same
consequence, different module and different owner -- which is exactly why sweeping stops at
neither.

INSTANCE 2 -- embed-core/vector.scala:71-76. The sharpest, and the tolerance is a THOUSAND
TIMES LOOSER than the align ones:

    val v = new ValidatedVector(dimension, normalization, values)   // built from the ORIGINALS
    case Normalization.L2 =>
      val n = v.norm
      if math.abs(n - 1.0) <= NormTolerance then Right(v)           // NormTolerance = 1e-6

`Normalization.L2` is not a description, it is a CLAIM THAT THE VECTOR IS UNIT NORM, carried
in the type. `of` accepts vectors whose norm is up to 1e-6 from 1 and stores them
UNNORMALIZED, so the type asserts something the value does not satisfy. Any consumer that
trusts the label -- skipping a normalization in a dot product because the vectors are
"already L2" -- inherits the error silently.

AND THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS TWELVE LINES BELOW. `l2(...)` normalizes and then validates. Two
doors onto the same type: one enforces the claim, one accepts a near-miss and records it as
satisfied. That is the ungated-sibling-entry-point shape from sweep 2, arriving in a module
sweep 2 has not reached.

NEGLIGIBLE, AND I AM SAYING SO RATHER THAN PADDING THE COUNT -- align/hsmm.scala:237,274.
Posterior rows are admitted when |sum - 1| <= 1e-9 and stored unrenormalized, which is
technically the same shape. The magnitude is logsumexp float noise, orders below any
precision we report, and renormalizing would add a pass over every row to fix nothing
observable. Recorded so the next person who greps 1e-9 does not re-derive it and file it.
Not a defect worth fixing; revisit only if a caller starts treating a row sum as exact.

THE CORRECT PATTERN, cite it in the fixes -- embed-grakern/distance.scala:324:

    else if math.abs(d) < Epsilon then Estimate.observed(0.0)

This ABSORBS THE ERROR INTO THE VALUE. It decides the distance is indistinguishable from
zero and then publishes zero, so the stored number agrees with the decision that admitted it.
Every instance in this family should end up looking like this line.

OCCURS UNMEASURED for both instances and I am not claiming it. Reading the branch establishes
permission, not occurrence.

Unassigned, unclaimed, I hold nothing. Related: bd-01M17AS0BGAW9CF6VFHST9JMY3 (three in
align/signature.scala) and scout's B2 fix at c4ed30e, which applies the tolerance to the
DIMENSIONLESS QUOTIENT rather than to absolute masses -- read that fix before starting either
of these, because the scale-dependence point generalizes and I had missed it.
